We have policy excerpts about rate limit: part 1: per API key, rolling window. part 2: burst can cause 429. part 3: X-RateLimit-Remaining and Reset headers show exact count. So answer: explain that the limit is per API key, rolling window, bursts count, and use headers to see actual count. Provide guidance. No mention of policy. Just answer.

function.arguments: {"message":"Hi! The 429s are coming from the rolling‑window rate limit on the API key. Even if you’re below the headline figure, a burst of requests can push the count up because the window counts the last 60 seconds continuously, not in fixed minute buckets. The best way to see what’s actually being counted is to look at the `X‑RateLimit‑Remaining` and `X‑RateLimit‑Reset` headers that every response returns – they show the exact remaining quota and when it will reset. If you’re still seeing 429s, try spreading the calls more evenly or check those headers to confirm the current usage."}

arguments.message: Hi! The 429s are coming from the rolling‑window rate limit on the API key. Even if you’re below the headline figure, a burst of requests can push the count up because the window counts the last 60 seconds continuously, not in fixed minute buckets. The best way to see what’s actually being counted is to look at the `X‑RateLimit‑Remaining` and `X‑RateLimit‑Reset` headers that every response returns – they show the exact remaining quota and when it will reset. If you’re still seeing 429s, try spreading the calls more evenly or check those headers to confirm the current usage.
